title: General Biology I
description: Build a rigorous foundation in cellular, molecular, genetic, and energetic principles of life while teaching students to reason from biological evidence, data, and experiments.

topics.title: Biology as a Scientific Discipline
topics.description: General Biology I should begin by teaching students how biologists ask questions, evaluate evidence, and build explanations from observations and experiments.

children.title: Scientific reasoning and experimental design
children.description: Students learn biology as an evidence-generating practice, not a list of facts.

children.title: Data literacy in biology
children.description: Students learn to read graphs, interpret variability, and connect quantitative evidence to biological claims.

children.title: Levels of biological organization
children.description: This gives a map from molecules to cells to organisms and populations.

topics.title: Chemistry of Life and Biological Molecules
topics.description: This unit establishes why carbon, water, weak interactions, and macromolecules make living systems possible.

children.title: Water and chemical context
children.description: Students learn why water, pH, polarity, and hydrogen bonding shape biological structure and function.

children.title: Carbon and functional groups
children.description: Carbon chemistry explains the diversity of biological molecules.

children.title: Biological macromolecules
children.description: Students connect structure to function in the four major classes of biomolecules.

topics.title: Cell Theory, Cell Structure, and Organelles
topics.description: Cells are the basic units of life. This unit teaches how cellular compartments divide labor and enable complex function.

children.title: Cell theory and microscopy
children.description: Students learn why cells are central to biology and how we know what cells contain.

children.title: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells
children.description: Comparing cell types clarifies what all cells share and what eukaryotes add through compartmentalization.

children.title: Organelle function
children.description: Students learn organelles as functional systems, not vocabulary items.

topics.title: Membranes, Transport, and Cellular Homeostasis
topics.description: Membranes define cells, regulate exchange, and allow cells to maintain internal conditions distinct from their environment.

children.title: Membrane structure
children.description: Students learn how phospholipid bilayers and proteins create selective, dynamic boundaries.

children.title: Passive and active transport
children.description: Transport mechanisms explain how substances cross membranes with or against gradients.

children.title: Homeostasis and gradients
children.description: Students connect membrane transport to cell survival and energy use.

topics.title: Enzymes, Energy, and Metabolism
topics.description: Life depends on controlled chemical reactions. This unit links energy, enzymes, and pathway regulation.

children.title: Energy and thermodynamics in cells
children.description: Students learn why cells require energy flow and how free energy predicts reaction direction.

children.title: Enzyme function
children.description: Enzymes make biological rates possible and provide points of regulation.

children.title: Metabolic pathways
children.description: Students see pathways as organized networks rather than isolated reactions.

topics.title: Cellular Respiration
topics.description: Cellular respiration shows how cells harvest energy from food and store it in ATP using redox chemistry and membranes.

children.title: Glycolysis and fermentation
children.description: Students learn how cells begin extracting energy from glucose and regenerate electron carriers without oxygen.

children.title: Citric acid cycle
children.description: This pathway completes carbon oxidation and loads electron carriers for ATP production.

children.title: Oxidative phosphorylation
children.description: Students connect electron transport, proton gradients, and ATP synthase.

topics.title: Photosynthesis
topics.description: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy and anchors most ecosystems' energy flow.

children.title: Light reactions
children.description: Students learn how pigments, photosystems, and electron transport capture light energy.

children.title: Carbon fixation
children.description: The Calvin cycle shows how atmospheric carbon enters biological molecules.

children.title: Adaptations and global importance
children.description: Students connect photosynthesis to climate, agriculture, and ecosystems.

topics.title: Cell Communication and Signaling
topics.description: Modern biology requires understanding how cells sense signals, process information, and coordinate behavior.

children.title: Signal reception
children.description: Students learn how cells detect external and internal cues.

children.title: Signal transduction
children.description: Students see signaling as cascades that amplify and regulate responses.

children.title: Cellular responses
children.description: Signaling connects molecular events to gene expression, metabolism, movement, and cell fate.

topics.title: Cell Cycle, Mitosis, and Meiosis
topics.description: Cell division explains growth, repair, reproduction, and inheritance. This unit clarifies how genomes are copied and distributed.

children.title: Cell cycle control
children.description: Students learn how cells coordinate growth, DNA replication, and division.

children.title: Mitosis and cytokinesis
children.description: Mitosis explains how genetically identical daughter cells form.

children.title: Meiosis and genetic variation
children.description: Meiosis explains gamete formation and why sexual reproduction creates variation.

topics.title: DNA Structure, Replication, and Genome Organization
topics.description: DNA is both a chemical molecule and an information system. This unit shows how genomes store and preserve biological instructions.

children.title: DNA structure
children.description: Students learn how base pairing and antiparallel strands support information storage.

children.title: DNA replication
children.description: Replication explains how genetic information is copied accurately before cell division.

children.title: Genome organization
children.description: Students see genomes as organized, regulated, and packaged systems.

topics.title: Gene Expression: Transcription, Translation, and Regulation
topics.description: Gene expression connects DNA information to functional RNA and proteins, making genotype visible as phenotype.

children.title: Transcription and RNA processing
children.description: Students learn how genes are copied into RNA and processed in eukaryotes.

children.title: Translation and the genetic code
children.description: Students learn how ribosomes convert nucleotide sequence into amino acid sequence.

children.title: Gene regulation
children.description: Regulation explains how cells with the same genome can behave differently.

topics.title: Mendelian Genetics and Inheritance
topics.description: Mendelian genetics gives students a quantitative foundation for predicting inheritance and interpreting crosses.

children.title: Mendel's laws
children.description: Students learn segregation and independent assortment as chromosome behaviors.

children.title: Genetic analysis
children.description: Students practice using probability and pedigrees to reason about inheritance.

children.title: Extensions to Mendelian patterns
children.description: Real inheritance often modifies simple dominant-recessive expectations.

topics.title: Molecular Genetics, Mutation, and Biotechnology
topics.description: This unit connects classical inheritance to DNA-level mechanisms and modern tools for reading and editing genomes.

children.title: Mutation and DNA repair
children.description: Students learn how genetic variation arises and why cells need repair systems.

children.title: Molecular genetics tools
children.description: Students learn the basic logic behind technologies used in modern biology labs.

children.title: Biotechnology and ethics
children.description: Students evaluate the promise and risks of genetic technologies.

topics.title: Evolutionary Foundations for Molecular and Cellular Biology
topics.description: Even in Biology I, evolution should appear as the framework explaining unity, diversity, and adaptation across cellular systems.

children.title: Variation and natural selection
children.description: Students learn how heritable variation and differential success change populations.

children.title: Molecular evolution
children.description: DNA and protein comparisons reveal common ancestry and functional constraint.

children.title: Evolution of cellular systems
children.description: Students connect organelles, metabolism, and genomes to evolutionary history.

topics.title: Lab Methods, Bioinformatics, and Research Skills
topics.description: A world-class intro course should teach students how biological knowledge is produced, measured, and interpreted.

children.title: Core lab skills
children.description: Students learn the practices behind cell and molecular biology evidence.

children.title: Experimental analysis
children.description: Students learn to connect protocols, data, and conclusions.

children.title: Bioinformatics literacy
children.description: Students get a first look at how modern biology uses databases and sequence analysis.

topics.title: Systems Biology and Societal Connections
topics.description: The final unit helps students integrate molecules, cells, genes, organisms, and society into a coherent view of modern biology.

children.title: Systems thinking
children.description: Students learn that biological outcomes emerge from interacting networks.

children.title: Human health connections
children.description: Cell and molecular biology explain many biomedical problems.

children.title: Biology in society
children.description: Students practice applying biology to decisions that involve ethics, evidence, and uncertainty.
